  "concerns": [
    "No rescue arm: without re-expression of shRNA-resistant KIAA1443 restoring proliferation, the 60% drop cannot be attributed to loss of the nominal target rather than to seed-based off-target effects of the two hairpins.",
    "Two shRNAs is not orthogonality — hairpins from the same library targeting the same transcript can share seed sequences and converge on the same off-target signature; the concordance of two shRNAs is weak evidence of on-target action, not strong evidence.",
    "Scrambled control alone does not control for the relevant confounder here. It controls for transduction/selection stress, not for off-pathway RNAi effects. A non-targeting hairpin matched for seed content, or a panel of hairpins with a dose-response in knockdown depth versus phenotype depth, is what the claim needs.",
    "No orthogonal modality (CRISPR KO, CRISPRi, degron) — the single most informative missing arm, and the one that would break the RNAi-specific off-target explanation.",
    "Antiproliferative readouts in glioma lines are the most promiscuous phenotype in cancer biology; a 60% proliferation drop is a low-specificity endpoint that many non-specific insults produce. No mention of whether knockdown depth was quantified at protein level, or whether the phenotype tracks with it.",
    "No demonstration that the phenotype is selective — no KIAA1443-low or non-transformed comparator line to show the dependency is not general toxicity.",
    "n = 3 biological replicates in one cell line panel from one operator, unblinded, unpublished, unreplicated externally. Adequate to detect a 60% effect; not adequate to establish attribution.",
    "The homology-model pocket is not evidence of anything in my domain and should not be read as support for the biology.",
    "As proposed, the next experiments are described as confirmatory ('that's on the list') rather than as a test that could return a negative and be believed. There is no stated criterion under which the PI would conclude the target is not the driver."
  ],
  "questions_to_ask": [
    "If you re-express an shRNA-resistant KIAA1443 in the knockdown cells, does proliferation come back? That single experiment tells us more than everything else on the list combined — has it been tried and failed, or just not tried?",
    "Across your hairpins, does the depth of the proliferation defect track with the depth of knockdown at the protein level, hairpin by hairpin? Or do you have a hairpin that knocks down well and gives a weak phenotype, or vice versa?",
    "Do your two shRNAs share seed sequence? If you pull them from different libraries or design a third with a deliberately unrelated seed, does the phenotype hold?",
    "What happens in CRISPR KO or CRISPRi — has anyone in the lab looked, even informally, and if the KO clones came out viable and proliferating normally, how would you interpret that against the shRNA data?",
    "Is this dependency selective? What does knockdown do in a line with low KIAA1443 expression, or in normal astrocytes — do you get the same 60%?",
    "Beyond proliferation, do you have any pathway readout downstream of KIAA1443 that moves on knockdown? A specific molecular consequence would do a lot to argue the effect is on-pathway rather than generic stress.",
    "In the public dependency data — DepMap, Project Score — is KIAA1443 a dependency in glioma lines, and does the pattern match what you see?",
    "What result would convince you the target is wrong? I want to know what the failure condition looks like before the work starts.",
    "The postdoc graduates in spring and is the only person who has run this — who reproduces the primary result independently, with fresh hairpins and blinded counts, before anyone builds on it?"

  "concerns": [
    "There is no chemical matter at all — no hit, no screen, no tool compound. There is nothing to assess for tractability, let alone a described route to a development candidate.",
    "Druggability rests entirely on a pocket seen in a homology model with no stated template, no sequence identity figure, and no apo/holo structure. A modelled cavity is not a validated ligandable site; it is a hypothesis that fails routinely at the HTS stage.",
    "KIAA1443 is an uncharacterised-name locus, which means the target family, nearest paralogs, and isoform landscape have not been named. Without that, in-family off-target liability cannot even be scoped — nobody knows which subtypes or isoforms a future chemotype would need to be selective against.",
    "No selectivity criterion exists because no counter-target has been nominated. Any future selectivity claim would start life as a homology argument, which is the weakest form available.",
    "No modality decision has been made or justified. If the pocket turns out to be shallow or a protein–protein interface, small molecule may be the wrong call, and the project would need to pivot to degrader, oligonucleotide, or biologic — each with a different and much longer timeline. shRNA phenotype is knockdown, not inhibition, so a degrader/ASO strategy may in fact be the mechanistically matched modality and small molecule the workaround.",
    "No tolerability or therapeutic-index information of any kind, in any species. Genetic knockdown in tumour lines says nothing about the consequence of systemic pharmacological inhibition in normal tissue, and glioma additionally requires CNS exposure — a brain-penetrant property profile constrains chemical space substantially and has not been contemplated.",
    "The 60% proliferation drop is a modest effect size for a monotherapy oncology target; a small molecule will rarely exceed the genetic ceiling, so the achievable pharmacological window may be narrower still.",
    "No costing, no timeline, and the only person with hands on the assay leaves in spring — the chemistry campaign has no starting point and no continuity of the biology that would guide it."
  ],
  "questions_to_ask": [
    "What is KIAA1443 actually — what gene family, what fold, and which paralogs or isoforms share the pocket you are modelling? I need to know what I would be selecting against before I can tell you whether selectivity is achievable.",
    "What is the homology model built on — which template, what percent identity over the pocket-forming residues, and is there any experimental structure of the target or a close relative? Has anyone run a ligandability assessment on that cavity, or is it a cavity-detection hit?",
    "Have you put any compounds on this protein at all — a fragment screen, a DSF or SPR pilot, even a handful of literature actives against the family? Is there recombinant protein and a biochemical assay, or is the shRNA phenotype the only readout you have?",
    "Does the phenotype depend on catalytic activity or on the protein being present? If a catalytically dead point mutant rescues proliferation, an occupancy-based small molecule is the wrong modality and we should be talking about a degrader or an ASO instead.",
    "Glioma means you need brain exposure. Has anyone thought about whether this target and its pocket are compatible with a CNS property profile, and what your target concentration in tumour tissue would need to be to reproduce the 60% knockdown effect?",
    "You see 60% proliferation loss with knockdown — do you have a dose–response from the shRNA or a degron system telling you what fraction of target you need to remove to get that effect? That number sets the potency and coverage bar the chemistry has to clear.",

    "What is known about the normal-tissue expression and any genetic-knockout phenotype for this gene in mouse or in DepMap non-tumour lines? That is the first read I have on whether there is any therapeutic index to work with."

{
  "verdict_signal": "caution",
  "concerns": [
    "The hub's question presupposes a 'ranking' or prioritization use case; what the PI actually has is a single unvalidated target hit, not a decision tool. In glioma, developers do not lack candidate targets — they lack targets that survive an intracranial, drug-exposed setting. Another in vitro proliferation hit does not change any developer's decision.",
    "Glioblastoma clinical practice has not moved on target biology since temozolomide (2005) and TTFields; the reason is not target scarcity but CNS delivery, intratumoral heterogeneity, and the fact that 2D patient-derived lines drift away from the in vivo transcriptional state. A 60% proliferation drop in culture is not evidence of a real unmet-need-closing mechanism.",
    "No indication precision at all. 'Glioma' spans IDH-mutant grade 2-3 (now served by vorasidenib, approved Aug 2024, and with slow natural history) and IDH-wildtype GBM (median OS ~15 months). These are different diseases with different trial designs, and the PI has not said which lines are which — vorasidenib's approval has already redrawn the IDH-mutant landscape and is standard-of-care drift that directly bears on this.",
    "No stated dependency on any patient-selection marker. Without a biomarker-defined subgroup, the realistic path in IDH-wildtype GBM is a large recurrent-disease PFS/OS trial with high attrition and no accelerated-approval hook — the most expensive and lowest-probability path in neuro-oncology.",
    "The PI does not know the competitive landscape, so the claim of unmet need is asserted rather than assessed. In GBM specifically, dozens of preclinically 'clean' targets have failed at phase 2/3; the base rate matters more here than in almost any other indication."
  ],
  "questions_to_ask": [
    "Which of your lines are IDH-mutant and which are IDH-wildtype, and does the knockdown phenotype hold in both? Vorasidenib's approval last year has changed what a new agent has to beat in the IDH-mutant population, so the answer changes the indication entirely.",
    "If this target were drugged tomorrow, who is the patient you would put on it first — recurrent IDH-wildtype GBM after temozolomide, or something narrower — and is there anything in the biology that tells you which patients would respond?",
    "Do the lines that respond differ from the non-responders in any way you can measure — MGMT status, EGFR amplification, target expression level? A dependency that tracks with a marker gives you a selected trial; one that doesn't gives you an unselected GBM outcomes trial.",
    "Have you looked at whether the phenotype survives in a setting closer to the tumor — neurosphere or organoid culture, or an orthotopic model — rather than 2D proliferation? In glioma that gap is where most targets die.",
    "Is the target expressed in normal brain, and at what level? In an indication where you have to get drug across the blood-brain barrier into a tissue you cannot afford to damage, CNS tolerability shapes whether this is developable at all."
  ],

}
